You don't have any Lincoln International items on file yet (invite, posting, or notes). The one step that starts a tracked prep is: paste the interview invite or the posting (or tell me the exact role, interviewers and format) so I can make a tailored brief and track it.

Short prep now — 10-minute plan and immediate mock:
1) Quick facts to know and say
- Role: Analyst (you said). Say one clear sentence: your current title, years of relevant experience, and one strength that fits M&A (modeling, financial analysis, transaction support, or sector experience). Fill [brackets] with your exact facts when you paste them.
- Why Lincoln International: pick 2 specific reasons (mid-market focus, cross-border deals, sector coverage you care about, culture of hands-on exposure). Have one brief story tying your background to each reason.
2) Top technical areas to expect and how to answer
- Financial modeling / accounting fundamentals: be ready to walk through a simple three-statement link, explain working capital movements, and how an acquisition affects goodwill and leverage ratios. Use concrete numbers when possible.
- Valuation questions: DCF mechanics (WACC, terminal value methods), comps selection logic, and precedent transactions rationale. If asked to value a company on the spot, state assumptions, show the steps, and give a clear sensitivity range.
- LBO basics: sources & uses, debt tranches, how operating improvements and multiple expansion drive returns. Be able to compute IRR conceptually with a sample exit multiple change.
- Excel / case tests: narrate your assumptions, keep math transparent, check edge cases (negative flows, zero growth).
3) Top behavioral/fit questions and how to structure answers
Use STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) and quantify results.
- Tell me about a time you worked long hours on a deal or project. Show ownership, list concrete tasks you did (models, decks, due diligence), and end with measurable outcome (closed on time, improved model accuracy, saved X hours).
- Tell me about a time you found an error in a financial model. Show the error, how you found it, steps you took to fix and prevent recurrence.
- Tell me about a time you managed conflicting priorities. Show prioritization, stakeholder communication, and the tradeoffs you made.
- Why investment banking / M&A and why Lincoln International? Be specific: mention deal types, sectors, transaction sizes you want to work on.

4) Questions to ask them (choose 3)
- "What does a successful analyst look like at Lincoln in the first 12 months?"
- "Which sectors or geographies are you expecting the most deal flow in next year?"
- "How do junior bankers get exposure to client management and transaction execution here?"
5) Quick on interview presence
- Speak confidently and concisely; answer the question asked before adding context.
